paper.title_en: Influence of $Δ$ resonances in hyperonic neutron stars on gravitational-wave inspiral signatures
paper.abstract_en: The composition of dense matter in neutron star interiors remains uncertain, with the possible appearance of the non-strange $Δ$ resonances providing an important source of theoretical uncertainty. In this work, we investigate the gravitational wave signatures of hyperonic neutron stars containing $Δ$ baryons within a density-dependent relativistic mean-field framework based on the DDME2 parametrization. Within this framework, the baryons interact among themselves via mesons. For $Δ$ baryons, the interaction is uncertain to date. We investigate how variations of the scalar and vector $Δ-$meson couplings, subject to \(x_{σΔ}-x_{ωΔ}=0.2\), modify the tidal properties and inspiral gravitational-wave signals. We find that the allowed variation in the $Δ-σ$ coupling leads to substantial changes in the tidal properties of the neutron stars, which in turn leave distinct imprints on the gravitational-wave waveforms, particularly in their frequency evolution, accumulated phase, and strain amplitude. These waveform differences arise through changes in tidal deformability and are not unique signatures of $Δ$ resonances. Future gravitational-wave observations may therefore constrain the $Δ-$meson couplings within the adopted dense-matter framework, subject to degeneracies with alternative EOS models.
